[[File:Hachioji Jinjya.JPG|250px|thumb|Hachioji Shrine at Fukazawa Mountain (Hachioji City)]]
'''Hachioji Shrine''' (八王子神社) enshrines the {{ill|lt=Eight Princes (Hachioji Gongen)|Hachioji Gongen|ja|八王子権現|1=Hachiōji Gongen|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/lt=Eight Princes (Hachioji Gongen)|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiōji Gongen|qq=}} (八柱の御子神) of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} (also known as {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}}). It is also referred to as '''Hachioji-miya''' or '''Yahashira Shrine''' (八柱神社), and there are numerous such shrines across Japan.

== Overview ==

Hachioji Shrines originated from the syncretic belief in {{ill|Hachioji Gongen|ja|八王子権現|1=Hachiōji Gongen|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Gongen|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiōji Gongen|qq=}} under the system of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}. 

In {{ill|913|en|913|qid=Q24860|lt=913}}, Buddhist monk Kegon Bosatsu Myōgyō had a vision of Gozu Tennō and eight princes while practicing asceticism at Fukazawa Mountain, currently {{ill|Mount Shiroyama|ja|城山 (八王子市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiroyama (Hachioji City)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11426084}} in {{ill|Hachiōji|en|Hachiōji|qid=Q208863|lt=Hachioji City}}, Tokyo. Inspired by this revelation, he enshrined {{ill|Hachioji Gongen|ja|八王子権現|1=Hachiōji Gongen|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Gongen|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiōji Gongen|qq=}} at Fukazawa Mountain in {{ill|916|en|916|qid=Q24886|lt=916}}.

Gozu Tennō, regarded as a Buddhist guardian deity, is believed to have had eight children with {{ill|Harisai-sho|ja|頗梨采女|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hariti|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1654753}}. These children are enshrined as the Hachioji deities.

The eight princes were later associated with eight directions and calendar deities, also known as {{ill|Hasshōshin|ja|八将神|1=Eight Directional Deities|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hasshōshin|13=User:Immanuelle/Eight Directional Deities|qq=}}:
* {{ill|Taisai-shin|ja|太歳神|1=Taisaijin|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisai-shin|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisaijin|qq=}} (Jupiter, Sōkō Tennō)
* {{ill|Daishōgun|ja|大将軍 (方位神)|1=Daishōgun (directional deity)|lt=Daishōgun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daishōgun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daishōgun (directional deity)|qq=}} (Venus, Maō Tennō)
* {{ill|Taion-shin|ja|太陰神|1=Taionjin|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taion-shin|13=User:Immanuelle/Taionjin|qq=}} (Saturn, Kumara Tennō)
* {{ill|Saigyōshin|ja|歳刑神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saigyōshin|qq=}} (Mercury, Tokutatsu Tennō)
* {{ill|Saiha Shin|ja|歳破神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saiha Shin|qq=}} (Saturn, Ryōji Tennō)
* {{ill|Saisetsujin|ja|歳殺神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saisetsujin|qq=}} (Mars, Jishin Tennō)
* {{ill|Ōbanjin|ja|黄幡神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōbanjin|qq=}} (Rahu, Takushin Tennō)
* {{ill|Hyōbijin|ja|豹尾神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyōbijin|qq=}} (Ketu, Jakidokikami Tennō)

During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} of the Meiji era, the eight princes were redefined as the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|ja|五男三女神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Five Male and Three Female Deities|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマテラスとスサノオの誓約}}, born from the {{ill|Oath|ja|誓約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宣誓|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q381045}} between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}} and Susanoo:
* {{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|ja|正勝吾勝勝速日天之忍穂耳命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q462555}}
* {{ill|Ame-no-Hohi|ja|天之菩卑能命|1=Ame no Hohi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Hohi|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Hohi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノホヒ}}
* {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津日子根命|1=Amatsuhikone|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アマツヒコネ}}
* {{ill|Ikutsuhikone|ja|活津日子根命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikutsuhikone|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イクツヒコネ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11147583}}
* {{ill|Kumanokusubi|ja|熊野久須毘命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumanokusubi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クマノクスビ}}
* {{ill|Takiribime|ja|多紀理毘売命|1=Tagorihime|2=ja|3=タキリビメ|4=fr|5=Takiribime|6=zh|7=多紀理毘賣命|1=Tagorihime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takiribime|13=User:Immanuelle/Tagorihime|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市寸島比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime||1=Ichikishima-hime|2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}}

Certain shrines enshrine different deities. For example, at {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine}}, the eight princes are identified as [[Yashimajinumi]], {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-kami|en:draft|10=fr|11=Isotakeru-no-kami|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-kami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-Mikoto1=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}, and other deities.

{{ill|11|ja|大将軍八神社|1=Daishōgun Hachi Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/11|13=User:Immanuelle/Daishōgun Hachi Shrine|qq=}} identifies the two as such

* {{ill|Taisaijin|ja|太歳神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisaijin|qq=}} ({{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|Ame-no-oshihomimi|qid=Q462555|lt=Ame-no-oshihomimi}})
* {{ill|Taionjin|ja|太陰神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taionjin|qq=}} ({{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵嶋姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichikishima-hime||1=Ichikishima-hime|2=fr|3=Ichikishimahime|4=ja|5=イチキシマヒメ|6=zh|7=市寸島比賣命|8=ru|9=Итикишима-химэ|10=de|11=Ichikishima-hime}})

== Origin of Hachioji City ==
The name "Hachioji City" originated during the Sengoku period when {{ill|Hōjō Ujiteru|en|Hōjō Ujiteru|qid=Q2790462|lt=Hōjō Ujiteru}} named his castle {{ill|Hachiōji Castle|en|Hachiōji Castle|qid=Q2969389|lt=Hachioji Castle}} after the legends of the eight princes.
